# Supply Chain and Third-Party Components (SUP)

Software Supply Chain Failures is new in the OWASP Top 10:2025 (A03). It covers every package, tool and vendor that our software depends on.

## SCS-SUP-01 Vet third-party packages before adopting them

Level: MUST

Applies to: All (Flutter and Backend)

Policy: Every new NuGet or pub.dev package MUST be reviewed before adoption for known vulnerabilities, maintenance status, publisher and license. Abandoned, unmaintained or known vulnerable packages MUST NOT be used, unless a documented risk acceptance is approved (see Exceptions).

Implementation (all stacks):

- Check the package in the OSV database (osv.dev) and GitHub Advisories, its last release date, number of maintainers, and open security issues.
- Prefer verified publishers and widely used packages. Pub points and download counts measure popularity, not security.
- Wait a few days after a new release before adopting it (release cooldown), as hijacked packages are usually removed quickly.
- Record new dependencies and the reason for them in the merge request description.

Implementation (Flutter):

- Avoid discontinued packages (pub.dev marks them); pin git: dependencies to a commit with ref:, and do not use dependency_overrides in release builds.
- Remember that plugins also pull in Gradle, CocoaPods and Swift Package Manager dependencies.

Verification: Reviewer checks the dependency diff (pubspec.yaml, *.csproj, Directory.Packages.props) in every merge request.

## SCS-SUP-02 Scan dependencies continuously and keep them patched

Level: MUST

Applies to: All (Flutter and Backend)

Policy: All direct and transitive dependencies MUST be checked against public vulnerability databases on every build and at least monthly. High and critical findings MUST be fixed within the timeframes in SCS-OPS-01. Runtimes and frameworks (Flutter SDK, .NET runtime) MUST be kept on supported, patched versions.

Implementation (all stacks):

- Enable Dependabot or Renovate alerts on repositories where the Git platform supports them.

Implementation (Flutter):

- Run osv-scanner scan source -r . (reads pubspec.lock) and dart pub outdated in CI; dart pub get also reports advisories. Justify any ignored_advisories.
- Stay on the current stable Flutter release.

Verification: CI dependency report shows no unresolved high/critical findings beyond their due date.

Current gap: IT-56 ASR-31 records only manual review today, and IT-57 §11 #2 lists automated scanning (Dependabot / Snyk) as planned.

## SCS-SUP-03 Lock dependencies and verify build artifacts

Level: MUST

Applies to: All (Flutter and Backend)

Policy: Builds MUST be reproducible from committed lock files, and only artifacts produced by the approved build pipeline MUST be deployed. Releases SHOULD include a Software Bill of Materials (SBOM). Base images, tools and CI actions MUST come from trusted sources and be pinned.

Implementation (all stacks):

- Generate an SBOM per release (for example CycloneDX: dotnet CycloneDX, or cdxgen for Flutter) and archive it with the release.
- Pin CI actions or tasks by commit SHA or exact version; do not share caches between untrusted and release pipelines.
- Archive each released build (APK/AAB/IPA, published .NET output) with its checksum.

Implementation (Flutter):

- Commit pubspec.lock for apps and build with flutter pub get --enforce-lockfile in CI.

Verification: CI uses locked restore; release folder contains the artifact, checksum and SBOM.

## SCS-SUP-04 Assess vendor and acquired applications before adoption

Level: MUST

Applies to: All (Flutter and Backend)

Policy: Externally acquired or vendor-developed applications MUST meet this organization's security requirements and be assessed by IT Security before purchase or adoption. They are not reviewed by the Security Reviewer under SCS-TEST-03. Vendors MUST complete a security questionnaire, provide evidence of secure development practices, and commit in the contract to security updates, vulnerability disclosure and breach reporting. Vendor deliveries MUST pass security acceptance testing.

Implementation (all stacks):

- Raise the request in Service Desk Plus with the intended use and data classification.
- Check before purchase: encryption, RBAC support, authentication (MFA, SSO with Entra ID / LDAP), logging and audit capability, and ISO 27001 / SOC 2 certificates where applicable.
- Contract/SLA: patch timelines, vulnerability disclosure, breach notification (aligned with the PDPL 72-hour duty), right to audit, source code escrow where appropriate.
- For custom vendor code integrated with our systems, require the vendor's security test and penetration test results during acceptance, and review the vendor's dependency list (SBOM). Code that this section writes to integrate with the vendor application is reviewed under SCS-TEST-03.
- Add the approved application to the application inventory.

Verification: The completed questionnaire, IT Security approval and the vendor's security test evidence are on file before go-live.
